blocks.title: First-Principles Core Truth
blocks.summary: Taxation divides into progressive direct taxes on income and regressive indirect taxes on consumption, unified by the 101st Amendment GST framework.

blocks.content: 1. Direct Taxes: Tax impact and incidence fall on the **same person** (Income Tax, Corporation Tax, Securities Transaction Tax STT). Progressive nature.
2. Indirect Taxes: Tax impact falls on producer/seller, but incidence is shifted to **final consumer** (GST, Customs Duty, Excise Duty). Regressive nature.
3. 101st Constitutional Amendment Act (2016): Introduced **GST** (Goods and Services Tax - effective July 1, 2017). Article 246A gave concurrent power to Parliament & State Legislatures.
4. GST Council (Article 279A): Constitutional body chaired by **Union Finance Minister**. Decision voting weight: Center $= 1/3	ext{rd}$, States $= 2/3	ext{rds}$. Majority required: **75% (3/4ths)**!

blocks.text:
⚡ 1. Direct vs. Indirect Taxes Feature Comparison
| Feature | Direct Taxes | Indirect Taxes (GST / Customs) |
|---|---|---|
| **Impact vs. Incidence** | Fall on the **same entity** (cannot be shifted) | Fall on different entities (tax shifted to final buyer) |
| **Progressivity** | **Progressive** (higher income bracket $implies$ higher tax rate) | **Regressive** (rich and poor pay same tax rate per item) |
| **Primary Examples** | Income Tax, Corporation Tax, STT, Capital Gains Tax | GST (CGST, SGST, IGST), Customs Duty, Central Excise |
| **Administrative Body** | **CBDT** (Central Board of Direct Taxes) | **CBIC** (Central Board of Indirect Taxes & Customs) |

📖 2. GST Architecture & GST Council Voting Mechanics
- **3 Sub-Types:** CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), IGST (Integrated GST for inter-state trade & imports).
- **Primary 4 Tax Slabs:** **5%, 12%, 18%, 28%** (Special 0.25% for rough diamonds, 3% for gold).
- **Items Outside GST Scope:** Petroleum crude, High-speed diesel, Motor spirit (Petrol), Natural gas, Aviation turbine fuel (ATF), and **Alcohol for human consumption**!
- **GST Council Voting Formula (Art 279A):**
  $$\text{Central Govt Weight} = \frac{1}{3}, \quad \text{All State Govts Combined Weight} = \frac{2}{3}$$
  $$\text{Decision Approval Threshold} = \mathbf{\ge 75\% \text{ of weighted votes cast}}$$

⚖️ 3. Common Prelims & Mains Traps
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** Neither Center nor States alone can pass a resolution in the GST Council! Center has $33.3%$ vote (can veto, but cannot pass alone without states); States combined have $66.6%$ vote (need Center to reach $75%$).
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** Alcohol for human consumption is **constitutionally excluded** from GST (requires a Constitutional Amendment to include), whereas 5 petroleum products are statutorily deferred.

blocks.content:
#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** What is the constitutional voting threshold required to pass a resolution in the GST Council under Article 279A of the Indian Constitution?  
(A) Simple majority (50%)  
(B) Two-thirds majority (66.6%)  
(C) Three-fourths weighted majority (75%)  
(D) Unanimous 100% consensus  
**Answer:** ** — Article 279A mandates a 75% weighted majority for GST Council decisions.

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** State A and State B vote together in the GST Council against a proposal supported by the Central Government. If 20 out of 28 states support the Center, calculate if the proposal passes.  
**Resolution:** Center vote $= 33.33%$. 20 states vote $= 20/28 	imes 66.67% = 47.62%$. Total weighted vote $= 33.33 + 47.62 = mathbf{80.95%} ge 75%$. The proposal **PASSES**!

#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Evaluate the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act 2016. Explain the voting mechanics of the GST Council and its impact on fiscal federalism in India.'*
